chapter: Learning the drums and early influences
title: Zutty Singleton, Baby Dodds and New Orleans drummers he never heard
summary: Crawford knew Zutty in New York, only knew of Baby Dodds, and did not hear King Oliver's or Armstrong's bands as a boy.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Now, did you -- during those years did you ever get a chance to hear either on record or in person Zutty Singleton or --
Oh, yeah, I knew Zutty well.
And -- where'd you meet him? Did you meet him before you got to New York?
I met Zutty, to be frank with -- no, I met Zutty here in New York.
You met him in New York. Did you know Baby Dodds?
I didn't know Baby Dodds, but I heard so much about him from New Orleans. Yes, I knew of Baby Dodds. They tell me -- Dobbs, it is -- what --
I knew of him. He was supposed to be during his heyday the most sensational drummer in New Orleans (inaudible). Oh, he was playing with King Louis Armstrong's (inaudible) King Oliver and all them.
Now, did you hear -- now, when you were like a kid in Memphis, did you hear -- did any of these guys come through Memphis and you get a chance to hear them, like
They may have come through there, but I didn't hear them. I didn't have the money to go hear them.
